mappings.note: Grey deposit on zinc but not on copper in iron sulphate; state the conclusion. The demand is the inference about relative reactivity (LO-2). Not C 8.2-LO-2 -- the investigation is handed to the student, nothing is designed.
Colour of a copper sulphate solution. A practical-observation item from the displacement lab, with no chemistry outcome behind it; cited at the inquiry competency C 8.2 rather than forced onto LO-2.
What is observed when zinc granules go into ferrous sulphate. Displacement, LO-2.
Which coloured strip is aluminium (silvery white). Identification by appearance, LO-1.
Iron nail in four sulphate solutions; only one gives a reddish-brown coating. Predicting which displacement occurs, LO-2.
Aluminium strip in ferrous sulphate -- the change observed. Displacement, LO-2.
The most abundant metal in nature. Occurrence, the front end of LO-6.
The most reactive metal in the series. LO-2.
The metal soft enough to cut with a knife. Physical property, LO-1.
A metal liquid at room temperature. Physical state, LO-1.
A liquid non-metal. Physical state, LO-1.
Fill-in for an amphoteric oxide. Oxide nature, LO-1.
Name for the elements and compounds in the crust (minerals). Ore vocabulary of LO-6. (The bank tags this 'Properties of Ionic Compounds', which is wrong.)
Which metal occurs free. Occurrence of unreactive metals, LO-6.
Sodium chloride is an ionic compound. Bond type from electron transfer -- the C 1.1 competency; no LO covers bonding.
Which metal gives hydrogen with nitric acid (the Mg/Mn exception). The rule being probed is metal-acid hydrogen displacement, LO-2.
Magnesium reacts with hot water. Graded water reactivity, LO-2.
The lustrous non-metal and the conducting non-metal. Exceptions to LO-1's physical-property rule.
Which listed property metals show. Options are not printed, but the stem fixes the subject as metal properties, so LO-1 is determined without guessing the key.
Which listed property metals do NOT show. Same reading as 104556: the subject is metal properties, LO-1.
Drawn into thin wires = ductility. Physical property, LO-1.
Beaten into thin sheets = malleability. Physical property, LO-1.
Which metals conduct heat poorly (lead, mercury). Physical property, LO-1.
What household wiring is coated with. Rests on the conductor/insulator contrast of LO-1.
Carbon as an example of a non-metal. Classification, LO-1.
All metals are solid except mercury. Physical state, LO-1.
Gallium and caesium melt very low. Melting point, LO-1.
The lustrous non-metal (iodine). Physical-property exception, LO-1.
Carbon's different forms are allotropes. Sits under the non-metal properties of LO-1; the frame has no allotropy slot of its own.
The conducting allotrope of carbon (graphite). Physical-property exception, LO-1.
Which alkali metal is soft. Hardness, a physical property under LO-1.
What non-metals (their oxides) give on dissolving in water -- acids. Chemical-property classification, LO-1. Stem is truncated but names its subject.
Magnesium burns with a dazzling white flame. Metal-oxygen chemical property, LO-1.
Metal + oxygen -> metal oxide. The general chemical property LO-1 classifies on.
Copper heated in air gives black CuO. Metal-oxygen reaction, LO-1; not LO-7, since this is heating, not weathering.
Formula of aluminium oxide. Writing a formula is valency work, the C 1.1 competency, rather than the property-based classification of LO-1.

Transfer item: brittle under the hammer yet conducting -> the graphite-style non-metal exception. Content is LO-1; combining two test results into one classification is the inference clause of C 8.2 (not C 8.2-LO-2, which is about two metals' reactivity).
Transfer item: liquid at room temperature but malleable when solid and conducting -> mercury, a metal. Same pairing as 150590, LO-1 plus the inference competency C 8.2.
A property of most metals. Physical-property classification, LO-1.
Name the liquid metal. Physical state, LO-1.
Compares metals and non-metals under four physical headings. LO-1 in full.
Assertion-reason on conduction and free electrons. The assertion is the LO-1 property; the reason is its atomic-structure explanation.
Fill-in for the only liquid metal. Physical state, LO-1.
The conducting non-metal. Physical-property exception, LO-1.
True/false on all non-metals being poor conductors -- tests the graphite exception. LO-1.
Beaten into sheets = malleability. Physical property, LO-1.
The most ductile metal (gold). Physical property, LO-1.
True/false on metals being drawn into wires. Ductility, LO-1.
Fill-in for ductility. Physical property, LO-1.
Brass is copper and zinc. Alloy composition, LO-7.
Defines an alloy and why alloys beat pure metals, including corrosion resistance. LO-7 exactly.
Stainless steel = iron, chromium, nickel. Alloy composition, LO-7.
Matches four alloys to their constituents. Alloying, LO-7.
Which metal displaces copper from its sulphate. LO-2.
Orders four metals by reactivity (LO-2) AND asks the student to describe an experiment that would establish part of that order, which is C 8.2-LO-2.
